chunks: His father - may God be pleased with him - narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoob ibn Yazid, who linked it up via his chain to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him),

that he (peace be upon him) said: "Enjoining good and forbidding evil are two of the creatures of God, the Exalted and Glorified. Whoever supports them, God will honor him, and whoever abandons them, God will abandon him, the Exalted and Glorified."
ai.seo_question: What is the theological status of enjoining good and forbidding evil in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq presents this narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) to elevate 'enjoining good and forbidding evil' from a mere legal obligation to a fundamental ontological category, describing them as distinct 'creations' (khalqan) of God. This theological framing underscores that divine honor and abandonment are directly contingent upon one's active support or neglect of these virtues, a concept central to Shia social ethics and the doctrine of the Minor Occultation.
